Objective data include information obtained from a veriﬁ able

Th e organization and content of the medical record will vary

amples of subjective and objective data, respectively.
A crucial skill necessary for conducting a nutrition assessment 
is the development and use of appropriate interviewing skills. 
Th e environment where the interview occurs, the rapport 
between interviewer and client, and the types of questions and
the manner in which they are posed directly aﬀ ect the quality 
and accuracy of the information that is obtained. Table 3.3 lists 
some basic suggestions for conducting an eﬀ ective interview in 
order to successfully gather nutrition data.
During the patient interview, information regarding appetite
and GI function should be obtained. Th is includes evaluation of 
the ability to chew, use and ﬁ t of dentures, swallowing ability,
nausea, vomiting, constipation, diarrhea, and heartburn, or any 
other symptoms that might interfere with ability to maintain 
adequate nutritional intake.
